decisions.summary: Every rule of the root CLAUDE.md - house style, research, development workflow, verification and iteration, session clones, what is enforced, key paths - is put to EACH of the twelve contracts one rule and one agent at a time, with no class of rule settled in advance; research.md holds a row per rule, a column per agent, each cell stated / moved / does not bear.
decisions.why: This is FR-001's own test ('read rule by rule against the contract') and FR-001's own record ('per agent, each rule considered and whether it was already stated, was moved, or does not bear'). Round 1's narrowing - a whole class of session rules declared to bear on no check - is gone: the plan now names the session-shaped work several checks do (perf-audit and the gate's bands with make perf-confirm, both fidelity agents running make figures, spec-fidelity recording make plan-verdict, settlement-review and size-audit running make targets) and says a rule about make, the gate, the clones or spec-kit is read against them like any other and may come out 'moved'. RESOLVED.

decisions.summary: Both nested files are read for every check that works under either tree, by a criterion rather than a roster: the skill's CLAUDE.md for every agent that reads or runs anything under .claude/skills/diagram/ (the five research agents, whose pages live inside that tree; entry-drift, whose subject is the interactive docstrings; both fidelity agents, which run make figures from there), and research/CLAUDE.md for every agent that reads under research/ (escalation-check among them). The table says per agent which tree it reads.
decisions.why: FR-001 asks for the same reading of the two nested files 'for the checks that work there'. Round 1's narrowing was a pair of disjoint rosters that left spec-fidelity, spec-fidelity-verify and escalation-check with neither reading; the assignment is now a behavioral criterion, both files may apply to one agent, the three previously dropped checks are covered by name or by the criterion, and the per-agent disposition is recorded. No check is excluded by construction, and a check that works under neither tree needs no nested reading by FR-001's own words. RESOLVED.

decisions.summary: A moved rule is written once, short, in the contract's own voice, in the section that already covers its subject, or under '## House rules you check against' where none does.
decisions.why: FR-001 asks exactly for the contract's own voice and no longer than the check needs; where it is placed is drafting.

decisions.summary: omitClaudeMd: true on its own line in each frontmatter, after effort:.
decisions.why: FR-002 asks for the field in the frontmatter of all twelve; the line's position is mechanical.

decisions.summary: A headless Sonnet session in the case's worktree is the dispatcher; it reads prompt.txt and dispatches the agent under test ONCE, and the SUBAGENT's transcript gives the reply, the turns, the usage per message id and the first-turn input.
decisions.why: FR-003 specifies this setting and leaves the dispatcher's model open; the dispatcher judges nothing and the agent under test runs on its own pinned tier. The recorded first-turn input per leg is also what makes the candidate legs - real agent FILES carrying the field - a check that the harness honors the field for a project agent file, which the spec's Assumption needs.

decisions.summary: Scoring is against the control first and the recorded findings second.
decisions.why: FR-003's standard IS the control ('the run with the field misses nothing its control caught'); the recorded findings are the second reference the spec also names.

decisions.summary: A run whose prompt was not handed over character for character is discarded and re-run, not scored.
decisions.why: FR-003 requires the recorded prompt verbatim, so a run that fails that precondition is not the specified experiment; the test is mechanical (result.json prompt_verbatim), not a judgment about the finding.

decisions.summary: Case directories from 251's seeded.py prepare; the control tree gets the clone's agent files with the field removed, the candidate tree with it.
decisions.why: FR-003 asks for each case run twice in the same setting, with the field and without; both legs carry FR-001's moved rules, which isolates the field as the spec intends.

decisions.summary: The record-format case is prepared with the pre-pass listing but WITHOUT feature 255's rejected scoped text.
decisions.why: FR-003 names 'the contract as it stands on main', and 255 R2 was NOT ADOPTED - the scoped text, its script and its target were left as they were, while make record-prepass is on main.

decisions.summary: P4 states the limit for P3: its worktree legs, candidate and control alike, run with no memory index, so the proof is of the CLAUDE.md files leaving; the index leaving is covered by FR-001's finding that no contract refers to it and by FR-006's measurement.
decisions.why: It is an honest statement of a limit the SPEC itself creates, not a narrowing of FR-003. FR-003 prescribes the setting ('a headless session in the case's worktree'), and feature 255 R5 measured that a scratch worktree is its own project and loads no index - so no plan honoring FR-003 can show the index leaving in a proof run, and nothing is being excused or skipped. The two coverers it names are the spec's own: FR-001 decides the index is not swept 'by the GM's words ... and no check's contract refers to the index (feature 255, R5)', and FR-006 is the before-and-after measurement. Writing the limit down is what the repository asks of an accepted limitation.

decisions.summary: FR-006's two legs are dispatched from /diagram, where the memory index loads, in 255 R7's probe shape: a headless session with the agent defined inline (--agents) from entry-drift's REAL frontmatter and contract body - its pinned model and tools - once as it stands and once with omitClaudeMd: true; nothing is written under /diagram.
decisions.why: FR-006 asks for the first-turn input of 'one real defined agent, dispatched from this repository before and after the field'. Round 1's narrowing was the worktree, which 255 R5 measured to load no index and so could not show half of what the feature claims; both legs now run at the one path where the index loads, on a real contract at its pinned tier, and the mirror is not written to (CLAUDE.md: /diagram is never a workspace; the open-task rule bars landing the field there first). The residue is named and covered rather than hidden: the inline definition leaves the harness's treatment of a project agent FILE to P3's candidate legs, which run the clone's real agent files with the field and record each leg's first-turn input. RESOLVED.

decisions.summary: entry-drift, the smallest real contract, is the agent measured; two short Opus runs because the agent file pins its model.
decisions.why: FR-006 asks for one real defined agent and does not name it; the tier is the agent file's, which is the point of the measurement.

decisions.summary: Root CLAUDE.md's review-subagents bullet gains one sentence; docs/efficiency-tooling.md's feature-255 row gains the outcome; docs/make-targets.html is unaffected.
decisions.why: FR-006 names those two documents and no other; docs/review-ledger.md is untouched as the spec requires.

decisions.summary: Constitution Check: no engine code, one shell harness under the feature's measure/, no guard file edited, tests/test_agent_models.py not touched, route DIRECT.
decisions.why: The delta is .claude/agents/, root CLAUDE.md, docs/ and specs/, which is the DIRECT route by the repository's own rule; leaving the tier test alone is what round 1 of the SPEC review required after the frontmatter guard was cut as unrequested.

decisions.summary: T01 reading -> T02 field -> T03 proof (six runs, plus FR-004's second pair if needed) -> T04 measurement -> T05 record -> T06 gates and landing.
decisions.why: It follows the requirement order and puts the reading before the field, as FR-001 and FR-002 are written; FR-004's second pair sits inside T03.
